attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post, stated as fact.

semantics.note: Faithful to the sequence. The proposition leaves out the reliability clause, but the contract keeps it as a component. The profanity is figurative.

contract.note: The plain readings of 'f* off', 'more pliant' and 'weak, loophole-laden' are ordinary and fair. Keeping the reliability clause as a factual component is reasonable.

evidence.note: Anthropic statement of Feb 26 showing it refused both uses. Its reliability claim is the company's own view, not an independent test.
Feb 27: Anthropic keeps refusing and reports Hegseth's supply-chain-risk move, a punitive response.
Verge report: OpenAI deal followed the blacklisting. Sources call it much softer, tied to 'any lawful use'. OpenAI's denial is noted.
OpenAI says its deal has more guardrails. That is a company assurance, not proof. Its March 2 update tightened the surveillance language.

reviews.rationale: The sequence holds: Anthropic refused, Hegseth answered punitively, and OpenAI then signed. Independent reporting supports 'softer' and loophole-laden terms on surveillance, though OpenAI disputes this. The reliability clause rests only on Anthropic's own statement, and no independent evaluation is in the packet, so that part is unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: 'It' refers back to the doomer hype ('all this'). The causal claim about enrichment, the lip-service description and the 'not yet delivered' AGI clause are all kept.

contract.note: The plain reading (publicity enriched companies through AGI expectations; safety conduct fell short) is ordinary. Keeping the financial metrics separate is appropriate.

evidence.note: Anthropic's $380B post-money valuation shows financial scale. It is a company disclosure and says nothing about doomer causation.
SoftBank has invested $34.6B in OpenAI at a $730B pre-money valuation. This shows scale, not cause.
Investor rationale tied to AGI expectations. It does not attribute those expectations to doomer publicity.
Anthropic reports safeguards it implemented and also softened some commitments. A self-assessment that settles neither side of 'lip service'.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows that large financing and AGI-linked investor rationales existed. It has nothing linking that enrichment to doomer publicity, no conduct-based test of 'lip service', and no AGI assessment. The causal claim is neither established nor refuted.

attribution.note: Part of Marcus's own earlier essay, which he republishes in a footnote and endorses.

semantics.note: The first-person 'hard-pressed to find' framing is kept. It is a softened report of his own search rather than a firm factual claim.

contract.note: 'Truly autonomously' and 'domain' have no standard. The result swings entirely on strict versus loose readings that the speaker never supplied.

evidence.note: June 2025 Project Vend: an LLM shopkeeper failed and needed help. A single company test that fits the strict reading only loosely.
Klarna's 2024 company claim, outside the period, with live agents still available. It does not contradict the claim.

reviews.rationale: This is a hedged first-person report with an undefined autonomy threshold. The evidence could fit either reading, so it cannot be scored.

attribution.note: Part of Marcus's own summer-2025 essay, which he republishes and endorses.

semantics.note: The proposition weakens 'no match' to 'outperformed', drops 'many domains', and leaves out the summer-2025 period. The contract puts back 'far worse' and the period.

contract.note: The plain reading (a large gap against specialised systems in several of the named domains) is fair and ordinary.

evidence.note: August 2025 Chess.com report: LLM chess strength is not close to engines.
June 2025: a 1979 Atari chess program beat ChatGPT 4o at beginner level.
January 2025 poker benchmark, before the target period and using older models.
March 2026 poker benchmark showing LLMs far below a solver. It falls after the target period.

reviews.rationale: Chess holds: in-period evidence shows LLMs far below even weak engines. Poker evidence falls outside the period on both sides, and there is no in-period evidence for logistics or navigation, so the 'many domains' generalisation is not verified. Nothing contradicts it.
